rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's proof lifts him above celestial objects and directs him to the Creator; its true source is God, not Abraham himself.
rows.anchor: bu hüccet nefs-i İbrâhim’in değil, Allah azîmü’ş-şân’ındır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raises whomever He wills by degrees; Abraham's elevation is part of a recurring divine practice among the elect.
rows.anchor: Mazhar-ı ıstıfâ-yı ilâhî olan ekâbir-i[^3] ricâlullahta bir sünnet-i câriyedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God granted Isaac and Jacob and guided them all; Noah had also been guided before them.
rows.anchor: hepsini hidâyete erdirdik, tarîk-i hakta muvaffak eyledik, emîn kıldık.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah struggled against idolaters and prevailed, making Abraham fortunate in the guidance of both his forebear and descendants.
rows.anchor: O da putperestlerle uğraştı ve onlara galebe etti.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “his descendants” naturally refers to Abraham, the subject under discussion, and initially suggests the listed prophets descended from him.
rows.anchor: Bu ذُرِّيَّتِهِۦ zamîrinin mevzû‘-i bahis İbrâhim olmak itibariyle ona râci‘olması, yani ber vech-i âtî on dört peygamberin İbrâhim aleyhisselâm zürriyetinden olması tebadür ediyor.

rows.speaker: birçok müfessirîn
rows.claim: Many commentators refer “his descendants” to Noah instead, since Lot was Abraham's nephew and Jonah was not Abraham's descendant.
rows.anchor: birçok müfessirîn bunu zikri[^5] karîb olan Nûh aleyhisselâm’a ircâ‘etmişlerdir.

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says all are affiliated with Abraham's descendants even when not biologically born from him, because an uncle is counted as a father.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas, “gerçi bu enbiyânın içinde Hazret-i İbrâhim’e

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Referring the pronoun to Noah avoids that interpretive extension, but shifts the passage's focus from Abraham to Noah.
rows.anchor: Nûh’a ircâ‘ı takdîrinde bu tevile hâcet kalmazsa da o zaman siyâk-ı bahis İbrâhim’den Nûh’a tahvil edilmiş olacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another valid construction links Ishmael, Elisha, Jonah, and Lot to the gift of Isaac and Jacob as support for Abraham, outside “his descendants.”
rows.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh وَإِسْمَٰعِيلَ وَٱلْيَسَعَ وَيُونُسَ وَلُوطًۭا âyeti وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُۥٓ إِسْحَٰقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ cümlesine rabt edilmek de câizdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This alternative is supported by the claim that one's own biological sons are not called descendants here and that Ishmael and Isaac form a brother pair.
rows.anchor: Ve fi’l-vâki‘insanın kendi sulbî evlâdına da zürriyeti denilmez ve iki birader olan İsmâil ve İshak tekabülü de bu rabtı iktizâ eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage names eighteen prophets in a deliberate arrangement centered on Abraham.
rows.anchor: Bu âyetlerde on sekiz enbiyâ zikr olunmuş ve bunların zikri bir hüsn-i tasnîfe tâbi‘tutularak Hazret-i İbrâhim etrafında cem‘edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah is the first prophet to confront idolaters, while Isaac and Jacob are the source of the prophets of Israel.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Nûh putperestlerle uğraşan ilk peygamber, İshak ve Ya‘kūb bütün Benî İsrail peygamberlerinin aslı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David and Solomon stand out as father and son with kingship; Job and Joseph stand out for trial and beautiful patience.
rows.anchor: baba oğul mülk ve saltanat ile mümtaz {وَأَيُّوبَ وَيُوسُفَ} ibtilâ ve sabr-ı cemîl ile mümtaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses and Aaron are brothers distinguished by miraculous power, majesty, scripture, and a special law.
rows.anchor: iki birader, kuvvet-i i‘câz, mehâbet ü satvet, kitab ve şerî‘at-ı mahsûsa ile mümtaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zechariah, John, Jesus, and Elijah exemplify asceticism, spirituality, and sacrifice.
rows.anchor: zühd ü rûhâniyet ve fedâkârlıkta misâl olmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although a report identifies Elijah with Idris, the author prefers identifying him as a prophet of the Children of Israel.
rows.anchor: İlyas İdrîs aleyhisselâm olduğu hakkında bir rivayet varsa da enbiyâ-yı Benî İsrail’den olması daha müreccahtır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elijah is reported as a descendant of Aaron, with a named genealogy; another view identifies him as Khidr.
rows.anchor: İlyas b. Yasin b. Finhas b. Azzar b. Hârûn denilmiştir. Hızır olduğu da söylenmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some reports say Elijah remains alive, as do reports about Jesus and Khidr.
rows.anchor: Îsâ ve Hızır gibi İlyas’ın da henüz berhayat olduğuna dair bazı eserler vardır.

rows.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan notes that Elijah is paired with Jesus and that both are described as not yet dead.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hayyân tefsîrinde der ki: “İlyas, Îsâ’ya mukārin olarak zikredilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jews and Christians call Elijah “Ilya”; in the Gospel account, “that Prophet” asked about alongside Elijah is Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets.
rows.anchor: “İlya” İlyas, “Ol Peygamber” de Hâtemü’l-enbiyâ Muhammed aleyhisselâm’dır.

rows.speaker: Râfizîler
rows.claim: The Rafidites also applied the name Ilya to Ali.
rows.anchor: Râfizîler tarafından “Ali” ismine de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the address is to the Prophet, Ishmael, his ancestor and counterpart to Isaac's line, begins another grouping; Elisha, Jonah, and Lot join him for their individual virtues.
rows.anchor: ceddü’nnebî olan ve İshak ve Ya‘kūb silsilesinin mukabilinde bulunan Hazret-i İsmâil diğer bir sınıfın mebde’i olarak buraya bırakılmış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some identify Elisha as Joshua son of Nun, but the source specifies Elisha son of Ahtub son of al-Acuz.
rows.anchor: Elyesa‘, Yûşa‘bin Nûn’dur diyenler olmuş ise de Elyesa‘bin Ahtub bin el-Acûz’dur diye tasrih ediliyor.

rows.speaker: Hamza, Kisâî ve Halef-i Âşir
rows.claim: These reciters read Elisha's name with a doubled lam.
rows.anchor: Hamza, Kisâî ve Halef-i Âşir kıraatlerinde lâm’ın teşdidiyle وَٱلْيَسَعَ okunur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Quraysh unbelievers reject scripture, judgment, and prophethood, it is no matter, since God has entrusted these to a people who do not reject them.
rows.anchor: Küffâr-ı Kureyş hiç iman etmezler ise hiç ehemmiyetleri yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entrusted people include the Medinan Helpers and people of Medina against Meccan unbelievers, other believing peoples against Arab unbelievers, and all prophets, Companions, Successors, believers, and even angels against unbelievers generally.
rows.anchor: ale’l-umûm kâfirlere karşı ale’l-umûm Benî Âdem’den peygamber, sahabe, tâbi‘în ve her mü’min ve hatta melâike

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those” are the chosen virtuous and righteous people granted scripture, judgment, and prophethood, whom God guided as in the security and guidance of 6:82.
rows.anchor: İşte yâ Muhammed! Bu zikr olunan ve ıstıfâ edilip kendilerine kitab ve hükm ü nübüvvet verilerek âlemîne tafdil edilmiş bulunan muhsinîn ve sâlihîndir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to follow their collective path of monotheism, faith, conviction, uprightness, virtue, beneficence, scripture, wisdom, and prophethood, without looking to others.
rows.anchor: bunların hey’et-i mecmû‘asının tuttukları tevhîd-i iman ve îkān, istikāmet, salâh, fazilet ve ihsan, kitab, hikmet, nübüvvet, hâsılı hidâyet yolunu tut, başkalarına bakma.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ha in the command to follow is a pause marker, not a pronoun; it preserves the preceding dal's vowel at pause and is normally silent in connected reading.
rows.anchor: Bu ٱقْتَدِهْ emrindeki ها zamir değil hâ-i sekttir. Yani hâlet-i vakıfta dal’ın harekesini muhafaza eden mücerred bir harftir.

rows.speaker: Hamza, Kisâî, Ya‘kūb, Halef-i Âşir
rows.claim: These reciters omit the ha in connected reading.
rows.anchor: Hamza, Kisâî, Ya‘kūb, Halef-i Âşir kıraatlerinde hâlet-i vasılda hazf edilir okunmaz.

rows.speaker: İbn Âmir
rows.claim: Ibn Amir treats the ha as a pronoun referring to guidance and reads it with kasra or prolongation when connected.
rows.anchor: Ancak İbn Âmir kıraatinde “hüdâ”ya râci‘zamirdir. Hâlet-i vasılda kesr ile veya med ile okunur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Abraham narrative is recalled to teach the Prophet to follow these examples, turn only to God, preach without fear or expectation, and seek no payment.
rows.anchor: Bunlara iktidâ edip yüzünü ancak Allah’a tut ve hiçbir şeyden korkmayarak ve başkasından hiçbir şey beklemeyerek teblîğ-i ahkâm et.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is a divine reminder and warning for rational beings everywhere, not for one person, class, or people; it is a universal mercy and reminder of what all need and owe.
rows.anchor: Allah için umûma muhtaç ve mükellef bulundukları şeyleri ihtardır, bir rahmet-i âmmedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are to eat what has been marked with God's name, which God has made permissible.
rows.anchor: Üzerine yalnız Allah’ın ismi zikredilmiş şeylerden yiyin ki Allah bunu size mubah kılmıştır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True belief in God's signs entails accepting this ruling, regarding this food as lawful, and following God's rule alone.
rows.anchor: Başka nâm tanımaz, hükmullahdan başkasına uymazsınız.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording indicates that the food must bear God's name, although not every item so named is lawful; the following verses specify the exceptions.
rows.anchor: مِمَّا ذُكِرَ buyurulması gösterir ki yenecek şeyler besmeleli şeylerden olacaktır. Fakat besmele çekilenlerin hepsi de yenebilecek değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next question challenges why anyone would refuse food bearing God's name when God has already detailed what He prohibited, except in necessity.
rows.anchor: üzerine ismullah zikredilmiş şeylerden neyinize yemeyeceksiniz?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition details appear in 2:173 and 5:3; this surah restates them at 6:121 and summarizes them at 6:145, with each passage reinforcing and explaining the others.
rows.anchor: Ve her biri yekdiğerini müeyyid, mübeyyindir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although this surah was revealed earlier, the other cited surahs precede it in the canonical arrangement.
rows.anchor: nüzûle nazaran bu sûre, tertîbe nazaran da öbürleri mukaddemdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many people mislead others without knowledge, relying on desire rather than evidence and divine law to label forbidden things lawful and lawful things forbidden.
rows.anchor: mücerred keyif ve hevâlarıyla idlâl ederler. Allah’ın hükmünü aramayarak ve O’nu bildiren bir delîl-i hakkı fikr ü mütâlaasına cidden esas tutmayıp

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone knows best who crosses the bounds of truth and will punish the transgressors.
rows.anchor: mütecâvizlere a‘lem olan, kimlerin hudûd-ı haktan bâtıla, helâlden harama geçmiş olduklarını en ziyade bilen ve -cezâlarını verecek olan ancak Rabbindir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to leave outward and inward sin covers public wrongdoing and wrongdoing whose evil is obvious even when concealed, as well as secret acts and hidden wrongdoing that needs evidence to recognize.
rows.anchor: Hâsılı “ism” günah, masiyet, kötü fiil demektir. Ve bunun bir zâhiri vardır bir de bâtını.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The outward and inward categories also cover bodily acts and inward sins such as disbelief, envy, and pride.
rows.anchor: Bundan başka bir fiil ya zina ya hırsızlık vesâire gibi cevârih ile yapılır veya itikadsızlık, hased, kibir gibi sırf kalb ile yapılır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every kind of sin must be avoided; those who earn sin will be repaid for what they have done, so hidden sin is not exempt from punishment.
rows.anchor: Ve bunların hepsinden sakınmak lâzım gelir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse lays down a general principle for prohibitions: they include hidden wrongs, not only obvious deeds that everyone readily recognizes.
rows.anchor: Bu âyet, ale’l-umûm ahkâm-ı hurmet hakkında bir asl-ı küllî beyan etmektedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many concealed harms cannot be discovered by unaided human reason; they become known through revealed law and divine instruction, so avoiding them requires adherence to the sharia.
rows.anchor: bunlar ancak şer‘in vürûduyla ve ihbâr ve irşâd-ı ilâhî ile bilinebilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelation clarifies lawful and forbidden things, while some matters between them remain doubtful and belong to hidden sin.
rows.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh وَبـَيْنَهُمَا أُمُورٌ مُشْتَبِهَاتٌ bu ikisinin ortasında şüpheli görülecek hafî bazı şeyler daha vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Doubtful cases should be resolved by ijtihad through clear, certain revealed evidence and a sound principle, setting aside the doubtful side as taught by the cited hadith.
rows.anchor: دَعْ مَا يُرِيبُكَ إِلىَ مَا لاَ يُرِيبُكَ medlûlünce

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even when the reasons for a prohibition are not apparent to everyone, believers should trust God's knowledge and obey His command, avoiding sin outwardly and inwardly.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın ilmine itimad ve emrine ittibâ‘ederek ismin zâhirini de bâtınını da açıkta ve gizlide gözünüzle ve gönlünüzle terk ediniz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command may extend to any food or drink on which God's name was not mentioned, though the author proceeds to restrict its legal sense to slaughtered animals.
rows.anchor: Bunun yenmesi, içilmesi melhuz her şeye âm olması ihtimâli yok değildir.

rows.speaker: Atâ
rows.claim: In one view, Ata applies the command generally: anything eaten or drunk without God's name is forbidden.
rows.anchor: bir kavlinde Atâ’nın bu umûma temessük ederek “gerek mat‘ûmât ve gerek meşrûbâttan her ne olursa olsun ismullah zikredilmemiş olan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other position of Ata and the rest of the jurists agree that the verse concerns slaughter; the later “I find no forbidden food” verse supports this reading.
rows.anchor: Fakat sâir fukahânın cümlesi ve diğer kavlinde Atâ dahi bundan murad zebh u tezkiye meselesi olduğunda müttefiktirler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, the relative “what” means animals conventionally subject to slaughter, and the prohibition concerns animals slaughtered without God's name.
rows.anchor: Şu hâlde ما mevsûl ve ahd-i şer‘î ile zebhi mutasavver olan hayvânâttan ibaret olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase covers three cases: carrion, animals slaughtered in another's name, and slaughtered animals on which no name was mentioned.
rows.anchor: Bu da zâhiri üzere şu üç şeye mütenavil olur:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Omitting God's name at slaughter may be deliberate or due to forgetfulness; the source calls these deliberate and forgetful omission of the invocation.
rows.anchor: Birisi ismullah hatıra gelmekle beraber zikri terk edilmiş olandır ki buna “amden metrûkü’t-tesmiye” denilir.

rows.speaker: İbn Ömer, İbn Sîrîn, Dâvûd-i Zâhirî
rows.claim: They hold that the literal wording also forbids meat when the invocation was omitted forgetfully.
rows.anchor: İbn Ömer, İbn Sîrîn ve daha bazılarından ve Dâvûd-i Zâhirî’den bu kavil mervîdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although carcass and meat dedicated to another are plainly included, the author says the wording's inclusion of deliberate omission is clearer and that forgetfulness prevents inclusion.
rows.anchor: göreceğimiz vechile nisyânın duhûlüne mâni‘vardır.

rows.speaker: İmam Şâfiî
rows.claim: Shafi'i prefers the clearer, more detailed 6:145, which does not specify omitted invocation, and therefore restricts this phrase to meat dedicated to another than God.
rows.anchor: İmam Şâfiî daha mufassal ve müfesser olan
